records.literal_gloss: And Joshua [was] old, advanced in the days; and said Yahweh to him, You [are] old, you have advanced in the days, and the land remains very much to possess it.

en.L: And Joshua was old, advanced in days. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "You are old, you have advanced in days, and very much of the land remains to possess.
en.B: Joshua had now grown old, far along in years. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "You have grown old and are far along in years, and very much of the land still remains to be taken.
en.R: Joshua had grown old. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "You have become an old man, and there is still a lot of land left for Israel to take.

sw.L: Na Yoshua alikuwa mzee, amesonga mbele katika siku. Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Wewe ni mzee, umesonga mbele katika siku, na nchi imebaki nyingi sana kuimiliki.

sw.R: Yoshua alikuwa amezeeka. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Sasa wewe ni mzee, na bado kuna nchi kubwa sana ambayo Israeli wanapaswa kuitwaa.

es.L: Y Josué era viejo, avanzado en días. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Tú eres viejo, has avanzado en días, y queda muchísima tierra por poseer.
es.B: Josué ya había envejecido y era de edad muy avanzada. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Has envejecido y tienes muchos años, y todavía queda muchísima tierra por conquistar.
es.R: Josué ya era viejo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Ya eres un anciano, y todavía queda mucha tierra que Israel tiene que tomar.

fr.L: Et Josué [était] vieux, avancé en jours. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « Tu es vieux, tu es avancé en jours, et il reste beaucoup, beaucoup de pays à posséder.
fr.B: Josué était maintenant vieux, avancé en âge. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « Tu es devenu vieux, tu es avancé en âge, et il reste encore une très grande partie du pays à conquérir.
fr.R: Josué était devenu vieux. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : « Tu es maintenant un vieil homme, et il reste encore beaucoup de terres qu’Israël doit prendre.

vi.L: Giô-suê đã già, tuổi đã cao. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với ông: "Ngươi đã già, tuổi đã cao, mà đất còn lại rất nhiều để chiếm hữu.
vi.B: Giô-suê bây giờ đã già, tuổi đã cao. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với ông: "Con đã già, tuổi đã cao, mà đất còn lại rất nhiều chưa chiếm được.
vi.R: Giô-suê đã già. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với ông: "Con đã già rồi, mà vẫn còn rất nhiều đất để dân Y-sơ-ra-ên chiếm lấy.

ko.L: 그리고 여호수아가 늙어 나이가 많이 들었다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 늙었고 나이가 많이 들었는데, 차지할 땅이 아직 아주 많이 남아 있다.
ko.B: 여호수아는 이제 늙어 나이가 많았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 늙어 나이가 많이 들었는데, 차지해야 할 땅이 아직도 아주 많이 남아 있다.
ko.R: 여호수아는 나이가 많이 들었다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 이제 노인이 되었다. 그런데 이스라엘이 차지해야 할 땅이 아직도 많이 남아 있다.

pt.L: E Josué estava velho, avançado em dias. E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe disse: "Tu estás velho, avançaste em dias, e resta muitíssima terra para possuir.
pt.B: Josué já estava velho, de idade muito avançada. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} lhe disse: "Tu estás velho e de idade muito avançada, e ainda resta muitíssima terra a ser tomada.
pt.R: Josué tinha ficado velho. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse a ele: "Tu já estás velho, e ainda falta muita terra para Israel conquistar.

decisions.choice: old, advanced in days: very old, near the end of a long life
decisions.reason: "Coming into the days" is a set way of saying a person has lived many years (Genesis 24:1, of Abraham; 1 Kings 1:1, of David). The same words come back when Joshua gives his last speeches (23:1-2). He dies at 110 (24:29).

decisions.choice: the land remains to possess: the conquest is not complete
decisions.reason: The summary in 11:23 said Joshua took the whole land. Here the LORD says much is still left. Both are true in their way: the power of the kings was broken, but many regions and towns were still held by their peoples. Verses 2-6 list them, and verse 6 promises that the LORD himself will drive them out.

decisions.choice: to possess it: to take it over and hold it
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession of land, which often meant driving out those who held it. The task left to Israel is to occupy what the LORD gives.

decisions.choice: left for Israel to take
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel as the people who are to take the land; the Hebrew leaves the subject unstated, but the rest of the speech makes it plain (verse 6).

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR" by default, "Yahvé" with the divine name setting ("El SEÑOR" at a sentence start, "del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé")
decisions.reason: For Joshua 13-24, as in the Pentateuch: the divine name is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", and the divine name setting gives "Yahvé". The span takes in the article and its contraction so both options read naturally. "Jehová" is a late form that joins the consonants of the name to the vowels of "Adonai".

decisions.choice: "que Israel tiene que tomar"
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel as the people who are to take the land, as the English Readable does; the Hebrew leaves the subject unstated, but verse 6 makes it plain.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("dit", "donna"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "a donné"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: As the French style guide and the Pentateuch note set for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. This holds for chapters 13-24.

decisions.choice: "posséder" (L), "conquérir" (B), "prendre" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to take land over and hold it. Literal keeps the plain "posséder"; Balanced says what it involves here, taking the land from those who hold it; Readable uses the everyday "prendre", as the English does.

decisions.choice: The LORD calls Joshua "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable; Joshua is "ông" in the narrative
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note sets for God speaking to a person: "ngươi" keeps the plain form of the Hebrew at Literal, "con" shows the closeness of the LORD to his servant at Balanced and Readable. Joshua, an old leader, is "ông" when the narrator speaks of him.

decisions.choice: "để dân Y-sơ-ra-ên chiếm lấy"
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, Readable names Israel as the people who are to take the land.

decisions.choice: The LORD speaks to Joshua in the plain style (해라체) with "너"; the story is told in the plain written style with the honorific for God
alternatives: the polite style for God's speech
decisions.reason: As the terms notes for Genesis and for Joshua set: narration in the plain written style (-었다) with "-시-" and "께서" for God, and God speaking to people in the plain style. This holds for chapters 13-24.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘이 차지해야 할"
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel as the people who are to take the land, as the English Readable does; the Hebrew leaves the subject unstated, but verse 6 makes it plain.

decisions.choice: tu (the LORD to Joshua, verses 1-7)
decisions.reason: As the book sets it (1:2; 7:10): the LORD speaks to Joshua with "tu" at every level, through the whole speech to the end of verse 7, so the commands are "reparte" and "divide" in the second person singular.

decisions.choice: regions: districts or areas
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "circle" or "round", and names a district (it is used of the districts of the Jordan, 22:10-11). Here it names the lands held by the Philistines along the southern coast.

decisions.choice: the Geshurites: a people in the far south, not the Geshur of verse 11
decisions.reason: These Geshurites are named with the Philistines and lived south of them, toward Egypt; David raided them from Ziklag (1 Samuel 27:8). They are a different people from the Geshurites north-east of the Jordan in verses 11 and 13.

decisions.choice: the land of the Geshurites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the land of" the Geshurites, so that the list stays a list of regions, as the Hebrew means.

decisions.choice: peoples as "Wa-" plus the name (Wafilisti, Wageshuri, Waavi, Wasidoni, Wagebali, Wamaakathi); places in the usual Swahili form ending in a vowel (Ekroni, Ashdodi, Ashkeloni, Gathi, Afeki, Diboni, Kiriathaimu, Yazeri)
alternatives: names copied unchanged from the English
decisions.reason: For the name lists of Joshua 13-21: a people takes the class prefix "Wa-", as Wafilisti and Waamori already do in the Pentateuch, and a place name ends in a vowel where Swahili writes one, with "s" for the Hebrew letter tsade (Suri, Safoni, Sereth-shahari) and the forms already used in Deuteronomy 2-4 (Aroeri, Arnoni, Heshboni, Bashani, Saleka, Edrei, Kinerethi). Every name in the lists is kept.

decisions.choice: "los guesureos" for these southern Geshurites
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads these Geshurites as a people of the far south, near the Philistines, not the kingdom of Geshur east of the Jordan in verses 11 and 13. Spanish keeps two forms apart: "guesureos" here, "guesuritas" for the northern people, as in Deuteronomy 3:14.

decisions.choice: "tout le [territoire] Gueshourites" with the noun in brackets
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "all the Geshurite", using the people's name for their land. French cannot put a plural people's name after "tout le" without a noun, so Literal supplies "territoire" in brackets.

decisions.choice: os gesuritas (as in verses 11 and 13)
decisions.reason: These southern Geshurites are a different people from those of verses 11 and 13 (m2), but the Hebrew gives both the same name, and so does the English; Portuguese keeps the one form, "gesuritas", and leaves the distinction to the meaning note. In Literal, "todo o gesurita" would not read as a land, so the words "[território dos]" are supplied in brackets.

records.literal_gloss: from the Shihor which [is] on [the] face of Egypt and to [the] border of Ekron northward, to the Canaanite it is reckoned; five rulers of [the] Philistines, the Gazite and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite; and the Avvim,

en.L: from the Shihor, which is east of Egypt, and as far as the border of Ekron northward, it is counted as Canaanite: the five rulers of the Philistines, the Gazite and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite; and the Avvim,
en.B: from the Shihor east of Egypt as far north as the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite land. There are the five rulers of the Philistines, those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, and there are the Avvim,
en.R: It runs from the Shihor stream, east of Egypt, north to the border of Ekron. All of this counts as part of the land of Canaan. There are the five Philistine rulers, of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron. There are also the Avvim.

vi.L: từ Si-ho, ở phía đông Ai Cập, cho đến ranh giới Éc-rôn về phía bắc, [đất ấy] được kể là của người Ca-na-an: năm vua chúa của người Phi-li-tin, [vua] Ga-xa và [vua] Ách-đốt, [vua] Ách-ca-lôn, [vua] Gát và [vua] Éc-rôn; và người A-vim,

vi.R: Vùng ấy chạy từ suối Si-ho, ở phía đông Ai Cập, lên phía bắc đến ranh giới Éc-rôn. Cả vùng này được kể là thuộc xứ Ca-na-an. Ở đó có năm vua chúa của người Phi-li-tin, cai trị Ga-xa, Ách-đốt, Ách-ca-lôn, Gát và Éc-rôn. Cũng có người A-vim nữa.

ko.L: 이집트 동쪽에 있는 시홀에서부터 북쪽으로 에그론의 경계까지, 그것은 가나안 사람의 [땅으로] 여겨진다. 블레셋의 다섯 통치자, 곧 가사 사람과 아스돗 사람과 아스글론 사람과 가드 사람과 에그론 사람의 [땅과], 그리고 아위 사람의 [땅과],
ko.B: 이집트 동쪽의 시홀에서부터 북쪽으로 에그론 경계까지인데, 이곳은 가나안 땅으로 여겨진다. 거기에는 블레셋의 다섯 통치자, 곧 가사와 아스돗과 아스글론과 가드와 에그론의 통치자들이 있고, 아위 사람들도 있다.
ko.R: 그 땅은 이집트 동쪽에 있는 시홀 시내에서부터 북쪽으로 에그론 경계까지 이어진다. 이 땅은 모두 가나안 땅에 속한다. 거기에는 블레셋의 다섯 통치자, 곧 가사와 아스돗과 아스글론과 가드와 에그론의 통치자들이 있다. 아위 사람들도 거기에 산다.

pt.L: desde o Sior, que [está] em frente do Egito, até a fronteira de Ecrom, ao norte, é considerada cananeia; os cinco príncipes dos filisteus: o gazita, e o asdodita, o ascalonita, o geteu e o ecronita; e os aveus,
pt.B: desde o Sior, a leste do Egito, até a fronteira de Ecrom, ao norte, terra que é considerada cananeia. Ali estão os cinco governantes dos filisteus, os de Gaza, Asdode, Ascalom, Gate e Ecrom, e ali estão os aveus,
pt.R: Ela vai do riacho de Sior, a leste do Egito, até a fronteira de Ecrom, ao norte. Toda essa região é considerada parte da terra de Canaã. Ali estão os cinco governantes dos filisteus, os de Gaza, Asdode, Ascalom, Gate e Ecrom. Ali estão também os aveus.

decisions.choice: the Shihor east of Egypt: a stream on Egypt's border
decisions.reason: The name means "the black (waters)". In Isaiah 23:3 and Jeremiah 2:18 it names a branch of the Nile. Here it marks the south-western edge of the land, and it may be the same as "the Wadi of Egypt", the dry stream bed that formed the southern border (15:4, 47; Numbers 34:5). "On the face of" Egypt means facing it, to the east.

decisions.choice: counted as Canaanite: part of the promised land, though the Philistines held it
decisions.reason: The coastal strip from the Shihor to Ekron was in Philistine hands, but it is reckoned as part of Canaan, the land promised to Israel (Genesis 15:18-21; Numbers 34:2-5). It is therefore among the land still left to take.

decisions.choice: the five rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: The word for "rulers" is used only of the Philistine leaders. Each of the five main cities, Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, had its own ruler, and they acted together (Judges 16:5; 1 Samuel 6:16-18). The Hebrew names the rulers by their peoples: "the Gazite", "the Ashdodite" and so on.

decisions.choice: the Avvim: an older people of the coast near Gaza
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 2:23 says the Avvim lived in villages as far as Gaza before the people from Caphtor, the Philistines, destroyed them and settled in their place.

decisions.choice: those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the city names instead of "the Gazite, the Ashdodite" and so on, which in English sound like single persons. Literal keeps the form of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the Shihor stream; counts as part of the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable adds "stream" so the reader knows the Shihor is water, and makes plain that "Canaanite" means the land of Canaan that God promised. It splits the long list into short sentences.

decisions.choice: "los cinco jefes de los filisteos"
decisions.reason: The Philistine title names the lord of each of the five cities. "Jefe" says that plainly; "príncipe" would suggest royalty. The cities in their usual Spanish forms: Gaza, Asdod, Ascalón, Gat, Ecrón.

decisions.choice: "princes" for the Philistine rulers (seranim)
decisions.reason: The word is used only of the lords of the five Philistine cities. "Princes" says they were rulers without calling them kings, which French "rois" would do.

decisions.choice: "vua chúa" for the five Philistine rulers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the special title of the lords of the five Philistine cities (meaning decision). "vua chúa" says they were rulers without making them kings of a kingdom; Literal brackets the "[vua]" Vietnamese needs before each city name.

decisions.choice: "통치자" for the rulers of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is used only of the lords of the five Philistine cities (meaning decision m3). "통치자" says plainly that each ruled his own city; the older "방백" is not current Korean.

decisions.choice: os cinco príncipes dos filisteus (L); os cinco governantes dos filisteus (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book and the books that follow (Judges 16:5; 1 Samuel 6:16-18). The word is used only of the Philistine lords (m3). Literal says "príncipes", a title of rank; Balanced and Readable say "governantes", which tells the reader at once that each ruled a city, as the English says "rulers". "Senhores" would be confused with "o Senhor".

decisions.choice: Gaza, Asdode, Ascalom, Gate, Ecrom; o gazita, o asdodita, o ascalonita, o geteu, o ecronita (L)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the five cities in their usual Brazilian forms, with a final "-e" or "-m" as Portuguese gives Hebrew names ending in a consonant. Literal keeps the Hebrew's names of the peoples; "geteu" is the usual Portuguese for a man of Gate. "Aveus" and "Sior" follow Deuteronomy 2:23 and the spelling of "Sefelá".

decisions.choice: from the south: read with the verse that follows it, or as a note on where the Avvim lived
alternatives: the Avvim in the south; all the land of the Canaanites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verse division separates "from the south" from the Avvim at the end of verse 3, and opens the next part of the list with it: the Canaanite land along the coast, from the south up to the land of Sidon. But the words can also be read with the Avvim, "the Avvim in the south", since they lived near Gaza (Deuteronomy 2:23). The sense of the whole is the same either way: the coastal lands from south to north are still to be taken.

decisions.choice: Mearah: a place name
alternatives: the cave that belongs to the Sidonians
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for "cave", and it may be read "and the cave that belongs to the Sidonians". As a name it is otherwise unknown. Either way it is a place in the land of Sidon, on the northern coast.

decisions.choice: the Sidonians; Aphek; the border of the Amorites: the far north
decisions.reason: The Sidonians were the people of the coastal cities around Sidon, in what is now Lebanon. This Aphek is a northern town, not the Aphek of 12:18 in the coastal plain. The Amorites here are the peoples of the land of Amurru in Syria, north of Lebanon, so the list reaches the northern limit of the promised land.

decisions.choice: the people of Sidon
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Sidon" for "the Sidonians".

decisions.choice: Meara
decisions.reason: Read as a place name, as the English reads it; the word is the ordinary word for a cave, and it may mean "the cave that belongs to the Sidonians" (m2).

decisions.choice: the Gebalites: the people of Gebal on the coast north of Sidon
decisions.reason: Gebal is the old Phoenician port later known as Byblos, north of modern Beirut (Ezekiel 27:9). Its land marks the northern part of the coast.

decisions.choice: all Lebanon toward the sunrise: the mountain country east of the coast
decisions.reason: The Lebanon here is the range of mountains inland from the coastal cities, together with the valley between it and the Hermon range. "Toward the rising of the sun" places it east of the land of Gebal.

decisions.choice: from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath: the northern limits
decisions.reason: Baal-gad lay at the foot of Hermon and marks the northern end of Joshua's conquest (11:17; 12:7). Lebo-hamath, "the entrance to Hamath", was on the way north toward Hamath in Syria and marks the northern border of the promised land (Numbers 34:8).

decisions.choice: the Lebanon mountains
decisions.reason: Readable adds "mountains" so the reader knows Lebanon here is a mountain range, not the modern country.

ko.L: 레바논에서 미스르봇마임까지 산지의 모든 주민, 곧 모든 시돈 사람이다. 나 자신이 그들을 이스라엘 자손 앞에서 쫓아낼 것이다. 너는 오직 내가 너에게 명령한 대로 그 땅을 이스라엘에게 유산으로 제비 뽑아 나누어라.
ko.B: 레바논에서 미스르봇마임까지 산지에 사는 모든 사람, 곧 모든 시돈 사람이다. 내가 바로 그들을 이스라엘 자손 앞에서 쫓아낼 것이다. 너는 내가 명령한 대로 이 땅을 이스라엘에게 유산으로 나누어 주기만 하여라.
ko.R: 레바논 산지에서 미스르봇마임까지 산지에 사는 모든 사람, 곧 시돈 사람들은 내가 직접 이스라엘 백성 앞에서 쫓아낼 것이다. 너는 제비를 뽑아 이 땅을 이스라엘 백성에게 나누어 주어라. 그 땅은 그들이 길이 차지할 땅이 될 것이다. 내가 너에게 명령한 대로 하여라.

pt.L: todos os habitantes da região montanhosa, desde o Líbano até Misrefote-Maim, todos os sidônios; eu mesmo os desapossarei de diante dos filhos de Israel. Somente reparte-a por sorte a Israel como herança, como te ordenei.
pt.B: todos os que moram na região montanhosa, desde o Líbano até Misrefote-Maim, todos os sidônios. Eu mesmo os expulsarei da frente dos israelitas. Tu, porém, apenas reparte a terra por sorteio a Israel como herança, como te ordenei.
pt.R: Todo o povo da região montanhosa, desde as montanhas do Líbano até Misrefote-Maim, todo o povo de Sidom: eu mesmo vou expulsá-los do caminho dos israelitas. Tu deves repartir a terra entre os israelitas por sorteio. Ela será deles para sempre, como eu te ordenei.

decisions.choice: I myself will dispossess them: the LORD will do it
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out before the verb, which stresses it. Joshua is old and cannot finish the conquest, but the land left is not lost: the LORD himself will drive out its peoples.

decisions.choice: Misrephoth-maim: a place on the coast south of Sidon
decisions.reason: The pursuit after the battle of the waters of Merom went as far as this place (11:8). The name may mean "burnings of water", perhaps from hot springs or salt works, but that is not certain.

decisions.choice: only allot it to Israel: divide it by lot now, before it is won
decisions.reason: The verb means "make it fall", that is, cast the lot (Numbers 26:55-56). Joshua is to give out even the land not yet taken, trusting the promise of the LORD. "Only" sets his task against the LORD's: the LORD drives out, Joshua allots.

decisions.choice: inheritance: land held as a lasting family possession
decisions.reason: The word names property handed down in a family. The land is given to the tribes and their clans to keep from one generation to the next (Numbers 26:52-56; 34:13).

decisions.choice: dispossess (Literal) / drive out (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb used of nations means to drive them out so that others take their place. Literal keeps "dispossess"; Balanced and Readable say "drive out", as elsewhere in Joshua.

decisions.choice: divide the land ... by lot. It will be their own land
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the land is divided by lot and explains "inheritance" as land of their own, in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "urithi" for the inheritance; "kura" for the lot
decisions.reason: For Joshua 13-24: "urithi" is the inherited share of land, as in the Pentateuch, and "kura" is the lot cast to assign it. Readable sometimes says "nchi yao wenyewe" (their own land) where the English Readable spells the idea out.

decisions.choice: "heredad" for the inheritance; "repartir por suerte" (L, B), "por sorteo" (R) for allotting by lot
decisions.reason: For Joshua 13-24, as the terms note sets: the land each tribe receives is "la heredad", the word for a lasting family holding, rather than "herencia", which suggests what is left by someone who has died. The lot is "la suerte"; Readable says "por sorteo", the everyday word for drawing lots.

decisions.choice: "desposeeré" (L); "expulsará" (B); "echaré" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "dispossess", taking the land from those who held it; Balanced and Readable say "drive out", as the English does. The same verb returns through these chapters (13:12-13; 15:63; 16:10; 17:12-13).

decisions.choice: "héritage" for nachalah (L, B), "leur terre à eux" or "leur part" at Readable where the English Readable says "their own land"; "le sort" for the lot
decisions.reason: The block's terms note sets "héritage" for the land each family holds for good, and "lot, sort" for the lot. "Héritage" keeps the link with the promise to the fathers; Readable says plainly what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "déposséder" (L), "chasser" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the legal sense of taking over what others held; Balanced and Readable say what it meant in practice, driving the peoples out.

decisions.choice: "sản nghiệp" (Literal, Balanced); "đất riêng" (Readable); "bắt thăm chia" for allotting by lot
decisions.reason: As the terms note for Joshua sets: "sản nghiệp" is land held as a lasting family possession, and "thăm" is the lot. Readable says plainly that the land will be their own, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (Literal) and "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (Balanced, Readable), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Both Vietnamese phrases already take in men and women, so the English choice between "children" and "sons" has no Vietnamese counterpart, as in Genesis.

decisions.choice: "유산" for the inheritance (*nahalah*) at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "길이 차지할 땅"
alternatives: 기업, the word of the older Korean Bibles
decisions.reason: The terms note gives "유산, 기업". "유산" is the current word for what passes down in a family; "기업" is the church word, but to most readers today it means a business firm. Readable says what the word means, land held for good (meaning decision m4). This holds for chapters 13-24.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L, B) and "이스라엘 백성" (R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: "자손" and "백성" already take in men and women alike, so the gender setting has nothing to change in Korean (style guide section 7). This holds for chapters 13-24.

decisions.choice: desapossar (L); expulsar (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verses 12-13). The verb is to drive a people out so that others take their land (r-en-1). Literal says "desapossar", to take a possession from someone; Balanced and Readable say "expulsar", as the English says "drive out".

decisions.choice: reparte-a por sorte (L); reparte ... por sorteio (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to cast the lot (m3). Literal keeps Numbers 26:55's "por sorte" in Portuguese; Balanced and Readable say "por sorteio", the everyday word, as Numbers 26:55 Balanced does. Balanced says "Tu, porém, apenas" to keep the contrast of "only" between the LORD's part and Joshua's (m1, m3).

decisions.choice: with it: with the other half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: "It" must be the tribe of Manasseh named at the end of verse 7, but the half meant here is the other half, which settled east of the Jordan (verses 29-31). The sentence turns from the land still to be shared out to the land the eastern tribes already held.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text kept as it stands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew passes very briefly from one half of Manasseh to the other. The ancient Greek translation has a fuller wording at the end of verse 7 and the start of verse 8 that describes the western land and then names the eastern half-tribe together with Reuben and Gad. A copyist's eye may have skipped from one mention of Manasseh to the next and left words out of the Hebrew, or the Greek may have filled out a short text. The Hebrew is followed here; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan eastward: east of the river
decisions.reason: "Across the Jordan" is said from the viewpoint of the land west of the river; "eastward" makes the side plain, as in 1:15.

decisions.choice: Moses the servant of the LORD: his title, as in 1:1
decisions.reason: The title marks Moses as the one who belonged to God and acted for him. The eastern tribes' land rests on his grant (Numbers 32:33; Deuteronomy 3:12-17), and Joshua does not change it.

decisions.choice: the other half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the half-tribe that "it" refers to, because "with it" alone would point back to the half-tribe of verse 7, which received land west of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal) / servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.

decisions.choice: "mtumishi" at Literal too, in "Musa mtumishi wa BWANA"
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch and Psalms, the title "the servant of the LORD" is "mtumishi" at every level; "mtumwa" would make Moses sound like a slave bought and sold, which is not what the title says. The English Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "el siervo del SEÑOR" at every level, Literal included
alternatives: "el esclavo del SEÑOR" (L), as the English Literal "slave"
decisions.reason: The terms note for Joshua, Judges and Ruth sets "siervo" for Moses's title at every level, as in Psalms: the Hebrew word names a servant who belongs to his master, and for Moses it is a title of honor (as in 1:1). Spanish "esclavo" would bring in the sense of forced labor; "siervo" keeps the bond without it.

decisions.choice: "Moïse, le serviteur du SEIGNEUR" at every level, Literal included
decisions.reason: The block's terms note keeps "serviteur" at every level for Moses' title, as in Psalms: it is a title of honour for the one who served the LORD, not a statement about slavery. The English Literal has "slave" here; French follows the note.

decisions.choice: passé composé at Literal in this verse ("ont reçu", "a donné")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is a plain past that looks back from the time of the share-out. French needs a tense of the past completed before the story's time; Literal uses the passé composé, Balanced and Readable the plus-que-parfait ("avaient reçu").

decisions.choice: "종" for Moses the servant of the LORD at every level
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "slave", but the terms note for Genesis keeps "종" for *eved* and "노예" only where slavery itself is the point. Moses's title is an honour, so "주의 종" is used at every level.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ của CHÚA" for Moses at every level
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note sets for this word: "đầy tớ" is the servant; "nô lệ" is kept for slavery itself. The English Literal "slave" has no separate Vietnamese counterpart here, since Moses' title is one of honour.

decisions.choice: Com ela (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's bare "with it", which points back to Manasseh in verse 7, though the other half of the tribe is meant (m1); Balanced and Readable name it, as the English does (r-en-1). Portuguese "ela" agrees with "a meia tribo".

decisions.choice: Aroer on the edge of the wadi Arnon: the southern limit of the eastern lands
decisions.reason: The Arnon cuts a deep gorge through the high land east of the Dead Sea and was the border between Moab and the land Israel took from Sihon (Numbers 21:13; Deuteronomy 2:36; 3:12). Aroer stood on its northern rim.

decisions.choice: the city in the middle of the wadi: a town in the gorge, not named
decisions.reason: The same unnamed town is mentioned with Aroer in Deuteronomy 2:36 and in verse 16. It may be Ar, the Moabite town by the Arnon (Numbers 21:15), but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the plateau: the high tableland north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: The word means level ground. It names the flat upland between the Arnon and Heshbon, with towns such as Medeba and Dibon (Deuteronomy 3:10).

decisions.choice: wadi Arnon, city (Literal) / Arnon Valley, town (Balanced) / Arnon River valley, town (Readable)
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that may run dry. Literal keeps "wadi"; Balanced and Readable say "valley". The word for "city" is used of any walled settlement, large or small; Balanced and Readable say "town" through these lists.

decisions.choice: Their land reached from ...
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence and supplies "their land reached" for the list that verse 8 opens.

decisions.choice: "korongo la Arnoni" (Literal), "Bonde la Arnoni" (Balanced), "bonde la Mto Arnoni" (Readable); "uwanda wa juu" for the plateau, "nchi tambarare ya juu" at Readable
decisions.reason: The same words as Deuteronomy 3 for the Arnon gorge and the high plain east of the Dead Sea, so the two books describe the land alike.

decisions.choice: "torrente", "ciudad" (L); "valle", "población" (B); "valle del río", "pueblo" (R)
decisions.reason: For Joshua 13-24, as in Deuteronomy: Literal keeps "torrente" for the wadi, a stream bed that runs only in the rainy season, and "ciudad" for the Hebrew word; Balanced says "población" and Readable "pueblo", since most of these places were small walled towns, as the English says "town". The plateau is "la meseta" (L, B), "la llanura alta" (R).

decisions.choice: "le torrent de l'Arnon" (L), "la vallée de l'Arnon" (B), "la vallée de la rivière Arnon" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 3:8: the nachal is a stream with the valley it runs through. "Torrent" is the usual French word for a stream in a steep valley that dries in summer; Balanced and Readable follow the English "Valley" and "River valley".

decisions.choice: "khe" (Literal); "thung lũng" (Balanced); "thung lũng sông" (Readable); "thành" (Literal) and "thị trấn" (Balanced, Readable) for a small town
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that runs only in the rainy season. Literal keeps the short word "khe"; Balanced and Readable say the valley, as the English does. Small towns in these lists are "thị trấn" where the English says "town", "thành" where it says "city".

decisions.choice: "골짜기" for the wadi and "성읍" for city or town
decisions.reason: "골짜기" names the deep valley of the Arnon at every level; Readable adds "강" so the reader sees that a stream runs through it. Towns are "성읍" and the open villages around them "마을" through the town lists of chapters 13-21.

source.text: וְכֹ֗ל עָרֵי֙ סִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלַ֖ךְ בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן עַד־גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

ko.R: 그 땅에는 헤스본에서 다스리던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼의 모든 성읍이 들어 있었고, 암몬 사람들의 경계까지 이르렀다.

pt.B: e todas as cidades de Seom, rei dos amorreus, que reinou em Hesbom, até a fronteira dos amonitas;
pt.R: Incluía todas as cidades de Seom, o rei amorreu que governava em Hesbom, até a fronteira dos amonitas.

decisions.choice: Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon: the king Israel defeated under Moses
decisions.reason: Sihon refused Israel passage and was defeated, and his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok was taken (Numbers 21:21-31; Deuteronomy 2:24-37; Joshua 12:2).

decisions.choice: the border of the sons of Ammon: the eastern edge, toward the desert
decisions.reason: The Ammonites lived on the eastern side of Gilead, around Rabbah (verse 25). Their border was along the upper Jabbok (Deuteronomy 3:16).

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the Ammonites" for "the sons of Ammon", the name of the people. Literal keeps "the sons of Ammon".

source.text: וְהַגִּלְעָ֞ד וּגְב֧וּל הַגְּשׁוּרִ֣י וְהַמַּעֲכָתִ֗י וְכֹ֨ל הַ֥ר חֶרְמ֛וֹן וְכָל־הַבָּשָׁ֖ן עַד־סַלְכָֽה׃

es.R: Incluía Galaad, la tierra de los guesuritas y de los maacateos, todo el monte Hermón y todo Basán hasta Salca.

vi.B: và Ga-la-át, địa phận của người Ghê-su-rơ và người Ma-a-ca-thít, cả núi Hẹt-môn, và cả Ba-san cho đến Sanh-ca,

ko.B: 길르앗과 그술 사람과 마아갓 사람의 지역과 헤르몬 산 전체와 살르가까지 바산 전체,
ko.R: 길르앗과 그술 사람과 마아갓 사람의 땅과 헤르몬 산 전체와 살르가까지 이르는 바산 전체도 들어 있었다.

pt.B: e Gileade, e o território dos gesuritas e dos maacatitas, todo o monte Hermom e todo o Basã até Salcá;
pt.R: Incluía Gileade, a terra dos gesuritas e dos maacatitas, todo o monte Hermom e todo o Basã até Salcá.

decisions.choice: Gilead, Bashan, Salecah: the hill country and the high plains east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead is the hill country east of the Jordan on both sides of the Jabbok. Bashan is the fertile plain to its north and east, toward Mount Hermon. Salecah was on the far eastern edge of Bashan (Deuteronomy 3:10).

decisions.choice: the Geshurites and the Maacathites: two small kingdoms north-east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: These peoples lived between Bashan and Mount Hermon, east of the Sea of Chinnereth (Deuteronomy 3:14; 2 Samuel 3:3; 10:6). They are not the southern Geshurites of verse 2.

source.text: כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וּת עוֹג֙ בַּבָּשָׁ֔ן אֲשֶׁר־מָלַ֥ךְ בְּעַשְׁתָּר֖וֹת וּבְאֶדְרֶ֑עִי ה֤וּא נִשְׁאַר֙ מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָרְפָאִ֔ים וַיַּכֵּ֥ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּרִשֵֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: all [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei; he was left of [the] remnant of the Rephaim; and struck them Moses and dispossessed them.

en.L: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei. He was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. And Moses struck them and dispossessed them.
en.B: the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last survivors of the Rephaim. Moses defeated them and drove them out.
en.R: It took in the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who ruled from Ashtaroth and Edrei. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim, a people remembered as giants. Moses defeated these kings and drove out their people.

sw.L: ufalme wote wa Ogu katika Bashani, aliyetawala Ashtarothi na Edrei. Yeye alibaki katika mabaki ya Warefai. Na Musa akawapiga, akawafukuza.
sw.B: ufalme wote wa Ogu katika Bashani, aliyetawala Ashtarothi na Edrei. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa watu wa mwisho waliosalia wa Warefai. Musa aliwashinda, akawafukuza.
sw.R: Ilijumuisha ufalme wote wa Ogu huko Bashani, aliyetawala kutoka Ashtarothi na Edrei. Ogu alikuwa mmoja wa Warefai wa mwisho, watu wanaokumbukwa kuwa majitu. Musa aliwashinda wafalme hao, akawafukuza watu wao.

es.L: todo el reino de Og en Basán, que reinó en Astarot y en Edrei. Él había quedado del resto de los refaítas. Y Moisés los hirió y los desposeyó.
es.B: todo el reino de Og en Basán, que reinó en Astarot y Edrei. Era uno de los últimos sobrevivientes de los refaítas. Moisés los derrotó y los expulsó.
es.R: Incluía todo el reino de Og en Basán, que gobernaba desde Astarot y Edrei. Og fue uno de los últimos refaítas, un pueblo que se recordaba como de gigantes. Moisés venció a estos reyes y expulsó a su gente.

fr.L: tout le royaume d’Og dans le Bashân, qui régnait à Ashtaroth et à Édréï. Il était resté du reste des Rephaïm. Et Moïse les frappa et les déposséda.
fr.B: tout le royaume d’Og dans le Bashân, qui régnait à Ashtaroth et à Édréï. Il était l’un des derniers survivants des Rephaïm. Moïse les battit et les chassa.
fr.R: Il comprenait tout le royaume d’Og dans le Bashân, qui régnait à Ashtaroth et à Édréï. Og était l’un des derniers Rephaïm, un peuple dont on se souvenait comme d’un peuple de géants. Moïse a vaincu ces rois et a chassé leurs peuples.

vi.L: toàn cả vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san, là vua trị vì tại Ách-ta-rốt và tại Ết-rê-i. Ông còn sót lại trong số dân Rê-pha-im còn sót. Môi-se đã đánh họ và đuổi họ đi.
vi.B: toàn cả vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san, vua trị vì tại Ách-ta-rốt và Ết-rê-i. Óc là một trong những người cuối cùng còn sót lại của dân Rê-pha-im. Môi-se đã đánh bại họ và đuổi họ đi.
vi.R: Đất ấy gồm toàn cả vương quốc của Óc ở Ba-san, vua đóng đô tại Ách-ta-rốt và Ết-rê-i. Óc là một trong những người cuối cùng của dân Rê-pha-im, một dân được nhớ đến là những người khổng lồ. Môi-se đã đánh bại các vua ấy và đuổi dân của họ đi.

ko.L: 아스다롯과 에드레이에서 다스리던 바산의 옥의 온 나라이다. 그는 르바임의 남은 자 가운데 남아 있었다. 그리고 모세가 그들을 쳐서 쫓아냈다.
ko.B: 곧 아스다롯과 에드레이에서 다스리던 바산 왕 옥의 온 나라이다. 그는 르바임 가운데 마지막으로 남은 사람이었다. 모세가 그들을 쳐서 쫓아냈다.
ko.R: 아스다롯과 에드레이에서 다스리던 바산 왕 옥의 온 나라도 들어 있었다. 옥은 거인으로 기억되는 르바임 족속 가운데 마지막으로 남은 사람이었다. 모세는 이 왕들을 쳐부수고 그 백성을 쫓아냈다.

pt.L: todo o reino de Ogue em Basã, que reinou em Astarote e em Edrei; ele restou do remanescente dos refains. E Moisés os feriu e os desapossou.
pt.B: todo o reino de Ogue em Basã, que reinou em Astarote e em Edrei. Ele foi um dos últimos sobreviventes dos refains. Moisés os derrotou e os expulsou.
pt.R: Incluía todo o reino de Ogue em Basã, que governava de Astarote e de Edrei. Ogue foi um dos últimos refains, um povo lembrado como gigantes. Moisés derrotou esses reis e expulsou o seu povo.

decisions.choice: Og, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei: the second king defeated under Moses
decisions.reason: Og king of Bashan came out against Israel at Edrei and was defeated (Numbers 21:33-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-11). Ashtaroth and Edrei were his royal cities (12:4).

decisions.choice: the remnant of the Rephaim: an older people known for their size
decisions.reason: The Rephaim were an ancient people of the land, remembered as very tall (Deuteronomy 2:10-11, 20-21). Og is called the last of them, and his great iron bed was still shown in Rabbah (Deuteronomy 3:11).

decisions.choice: them: Sihon and Og with their peoples
decisions.reason: "Them" goes back over verses 10-12 to the two kings and the peoples of their kingdoms. Moses defeated both and Israel took their land.

decisions.choice: a people remembered as giants; these kings and ... their people
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Rephaim were, as m2 does, and says who "them" are.

decisions.choice: "un pueblo que se recordaba como de gigantes"; "a estos reyes ... a su gente"
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Rephaim were and says whom Moses defeated and drove out, as the English Readable does (meaning decisions m2, m3).

decisions.choice: "거인으로 기억되는 르바임 족속"; "이 왕들을 ... 그 백성을"
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Rephaim were and whom Moses defeated (meaning decisions m2 and m3), as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְלֹ֤א הוֹרִ֨ישׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־הַגְּשׁוּרִ֖י וְאֶת־הַמַּעֲכָתִ֑י וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב גְּשׁ֤וּר וּמַֽעֲכָת֙ בְּקֶ֣רֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: But not dispossessed [the] sons of Israel the Geshurite and the Maacathite; and dwells Geshur and Maacath in [the] midst of Israel until the day the this.

en.L: But the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did not dispossess the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath live in the midst of Israel to this day.
en.B: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did not drive out the Geshurites and the Maacathites, so Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.
en.R: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did not drive out the people of Geshur and Maacath. They still live among the Israelites today.

sw.L: Lakini wana wa Israeli hawakuwafukuza Wageshuri na Wamaakathi; na Geshuri na Maakathi wanakaa katikati ya Israeli hadi siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Lakini Waisraeli hawakuwafukuza Wageshuri na Wamaakathi, kwa hiyo Geshuri na Maakathi wanaishi kati ya Israeli mpaka leo.
sw.R: Lakini Waisraeli hawakuwafukuza watu wa Geshuri na Maakathi. Bado wanaishi kati ya Waisraeli hata leo.

es.L: Pero los hijos de Israel no desposeyeron a los guesuritas ni a los maacateos, y Guesur y Maacá habitan en medio de Israel hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Pero los israelitas no expulsaron a los guesuritas ni a los maacateos, así que Guesur y Maacá viven en medio de Israel hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Pero los israelitas no echaron a la gente de Guesur y Maacá. Todavía hoy viven entre los israelitas.

fr.L: Mais les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ne dépossédèrent pas les Gueshourites et les Maakatites, et Gueshour et Maakath habitent au milieu d’Israël jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ne chassèrent pas les Gueshourites et les Maakatites, si bien que Gueshour et Maakath habitent au milieu d’Israël jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.R: Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} n’ont pas chassé les habitants de Gueshour et de Maakath. Ils vivent encore aujourd’hui au milieu des Israélites.

vi.L: Nhưng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên không đuổi người Ghê-su-rơ và người Ma-a-ca-thít đi, nên Ghê-su-rơ và Ma-a-cát sống giữa Y-sơ-ra-ên cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Nhưng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã không đuổi người Ghê-su-rơ và người Ma-a-ca-thít đi, nên Ghê-su-rơ và Ma-a-cát vẫn sống giữa Y-sơ-ra-ên cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Nhưng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên không đuổi dân Ghê-su-rơ và dân Ma-a-cát đi. Họ vẫn còn sống giữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên cho đến ngày nay.

ko.L: 그러나 이스라엘 자손이 그술 사람과 마아갓 사람을 쫓아내지 않았다. 그래서 그술과 마아갓이 오늘까지 이스라엘 가운데 살고 있다.
ko.B: 그러나 이스라엘 자손은 그술 사람과 마아갓 사람을 쫓아내지 않았으므로, 그술과 마아갓은 오늘까지 이스라엘 가운데서 살고 있다.
ko.R: 그러나 이스라엘 백성은 그술과 마아갓 사람들을 쫓아내지 않았다. 그래서 그들은 지금도 이스라엘 백성 가운데서 살고 있다.

pt.L: Mas os filhos de Israel não desapossaram os gesuritas e os maacatitas, e Gesur e Maacate habitam no meio de Israel até este dia.
pt.B: Mas os israelitas não expulsaram os gesuritas e os maacatitas, e por isso Gesur e Maacate vivem no meio de Israel até hoje.
pt.R: Mas os israelitas não expulsaram o povo de Gesur e de Maacate. Eles ainda hoje vivem no meio dos israelitas.

decisions.choice: did not dispossess: a task left undone
decisions.reason: The book notes several peoples that Israel did not drive out (15:63; 16:10; 17:12-13). Here it is the two small kingdoms of verse 11. Later David married a daughter of the king of Geshur (2 Samuel 3:3).

decisions.choice: Geshur and Maacath: the two peoples named by their lands
decisions.reason: The names of the lands stand for their peoples. "Maacath" is the form used here for the land elsewhere called Maacah (2 Samuel 10:6).

decisions.choice: to this day: to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The writer speaks from a later time and notes that the situation still holds (as in 4:9; 5:9).

decisions.choice: dispossess (Literal) / drive out (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: For Joshua 13-24, as in the Pentateuch: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters, so the Literal "los hijos de Israel" is inclusive as it stands, and Balanced and Readable say "los israelitas". Spanish has no second wording for the gender setting to change. The same holds for "los hijos de Judá", "los descendientes de José" and the other tribes.

source.text: רַ֚ק לְשֵׁ֣בֶט הַלֵּוִ֔י לֹ֥א נָתַ֖ן נַחֲלָ֑ה אִשֵּׁ֨י יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־לֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Only to [the] tribe of the Levi not he gave an inheritance; [the] offerings by fire of Yahweh, God of Israel, it [is] his inheritance, just as he spoke to him.

en.L: Only to the tribe of Levi he did not give an inheritance; the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to it.
en.B: Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The food offerings of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised it.
en.R: But Moses gave no land to the tribe of Levi. Instead, the food offerings burned for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, are their share, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them.

sw.L: Ila kabila la Lawi hakulipa urithi; sadaka za kuteketezwa kwa moto za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, ndizo urithi wake, kama alivyoliambia.
sw.B: Ila kabila la Lawi hakulipa urithi. Sadaka za kuteketezwa kwa moto za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, ndizo urithi wake, kama alivyoliahidi.
sw.R: Lakini Musa hakulipa kabila la Lawi nchi. Badala yake, sadaka zinazoteketezwa kwa moto kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, ndizo fungu lao, kama alivyowaahidi.

es.L: Solo a la tribu de Leví no le dio heredad; las ofrendas quemadas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, son su heredad, tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le había dicho.
es.B: Solo a la tribu de Leví no le dio heredad. Las ofrendas quemadas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, son su heredad, como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se lo prometió.
es.R: Pero Moisés no le dio tierra a la tribu de Leví. En cambio, las ofrendas que se queman para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, son su parte, como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se lo prometió.

fr.L: Seulement, à la tribu de Lévi il ne donna pas d’héritage ; les offrandes consumées par le feu {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, c’est son héritage, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le lui a dit.
fr.B: Seule la tribu de Lévi ne reçut de lui aucun héritage. Les offrandes consumées par le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, voilà son héritage, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le lui avait promis.
fr.R: Mais Moïse n’a pas donné de terre à la tribu de Lévi. À la place, les offrandes brûlées pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, sont leur part, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le leur avait promis.

vi.L: Chỉ có chi tộc Lê-vi là ông không ban cho sản nghiệp; các lễ vật dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, là sản nghiệp của chi tộc ấy, đúng như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán với họ.
vi.B: Chỉ có chi tộc Lê-vi là ông không ban cho sản nghiệp. Các lễ vật dâng làm thức ăn cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, là sản nghiệp của chi tộc ấy, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hứa với họ.
vi.R: Nhưng Môi-se không ban đất cho chi tộc Lê-vi. Thay vào đó, các lễ vật được đốt dâng lên {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, là phần của họ, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hứa với họ.

ko.L: 오직 레위 지파에게는 그가 유산을 주지 않았다. 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 화제물이 그들의 유산이니, 그분께서 그들에게 말씀하신 대로이다.
ko.B: 다만 레위 지파에게는 모세가 유산을 주지 않았다. 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바치는 음식 제물이 그들의 유산이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 약속하신 대로이다.
ko.R: 그러나 모세는 레위 지파에게는 땅을 주지 않았다. 그 대신 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불살라 바치는 음식 제물이 그들의 몫이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 그렇게 약속하셨다.

pt.L: Somente à tribo de Levi ele não deu herança; as ofertas queimadas {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, são a sua herança, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe falou.
pt.B: Somente à tribo de Levi ele não deu herança. As ofertas queimadas {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, são a sua herança, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe prometeu.
pt.R: Mas Moisés não deu terra à tribo de Levi. Em vez disso, as ofertas queimadas para {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, são a parte que cabe aos levitas, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes prometeu.

decisions.choice: he did not give: Moses
decisions.reason: The subject is not named, but it is Moses, who gave the eastern lands (verses 8 and 15), as verse 33 says outright.

decisions.choice: no inheritance for Levi: the tribe received towns, not a territory
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi served at the sanctuary and received no share of the land. It was given towns to live in, with pasture around them (chapter 21; Numbers 35:1-8).

decisions.choice: the offerings by fire of the LORD: the gifts brought to the LORD at the altar
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 18:1. Parts of many offerings went to the priests and Levites as food, and these, with the tithes, were how the tribe lived (Numbers 18:8-24).

decisions.choice: as he promised it: the LORD's word to Aaron and Levi
decisions.reason: The LORD said that he himself would be Levi's share among Israel (Numbers 18:20; Deuteronomy 10:9; 18:2). "It" and "its" refer to the tribe, which the Hebrew speaks of as one person ("him", "his").

decisions.choice: offerings by fire (Literal) / food offerings (Balanced) / food offerings burned (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 18:1.

decisions.choice: Moses; their; them
decisions.reason: Readable names Moses as the one who gave the land, and speaks of the tribe as "they", which is more natural in English than "it".

decisions.choice: "sadaka za kuteketezwa kwa moto" at every level
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note fixes this word for the offerings given to the LORD by fire. The English Balanced says "food offerings"; Swahili keeps one term, which already says what the offerings were.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span for "he promised"
decisions.reason: Swahili puts the pronoun for God inside the verb ("alivyoliahidi"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting has nothing to change here. In these chapters a span appears only on a free pronoun for God ("yeye", "wake", "naye").

decisions.choice: "las ofrendas quemadas" (L, B); "las ofrendas que se queman para el SEÑOR" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms list sets for this Hebrew word: the gifts burned on the altar for the LORD, part of which fed the priests and Levites. Readable unfolds the phrase as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "les offrandes consumées par le feu" (L, B), "les offrandes brûlées" (R)
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note sets "l'offrande consumée par le feu" for the ishsheh, the gifts burned on the altar of which the priests received a share. Readable uses the shorter "brûlées".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; "그분께서" (L) or the name again (B, R), with the honorific
decisions.reason: Hangul has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Where the English has "he" for God, Korean says "그분께서" or names the LORD again, and the honorific shows who acts (style guide section 7). This holds for chapters 13-24.

decisions.choice: "화제물" (L); "음식 제물" (B); "불살라 바치는 음식 제물" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the offering "by fire", in the word of the older Korean Bibles; Balanced and Readable say what the offering was, food given to the LORD on the altar, as the English Balanced and Readable do. Balanced and Readable name Moses as the giver (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "lễ vật dâng bằng lửa" (Literal); "lễ vật dâng làm thức ăn" (Balanced); "lễ vật được đốt dâng lên" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is linked with fire and with food given to the LORD at the altar (meaning decision); each level keeps the side the English level keeps. "họ" for the tribe reads more naturally in Vietnamese than "it".

decisions.choice: as ofertas queimadas (every level)
decisions.reason: As Deuteronomy 18:1 has it in Portuguese, and as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets for this word: "ofertas queimadas" at every level, where the English says "offerings by fire" and "food offerings"; Readable names the Levites as the ones whose share it is, as the English Readable says "their".

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־רְאוּבֵ֖ן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Moses to [the] tribe of [the] sons of Reuben according to their clans.

en.L: And Moses gave to the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their clans.
en.B: Moses gave land to the tribe of the descendants of Reuben, clan by clan.
en.R: Moses gave land to the tribe of Reuben, family by family.

sw.L: Na Musa akalipa kabila la wana wa Reubeni kufuatana na koo zao.
sw.B: Musa alilipa kabila la wazao wa Reubeni nchi, ukoo kwa ukoo.
sw.R: Musa aliwapa kabila la Reubeni nchi, jamaa kwa jamaa.

es.L: Y Moisés dio a la tribu de los hijos de Rubén conforme a sus clanes.
es.B: Moisés dio tierra a la tribu de los descendientes de Rubén, clan por clan.
es.R: Moisés le dio tierra a la tribu de Rubén, familia por familia.

fr.L: Et Moïse donna à la tribu des fils de Ruben selon leurs clans.
fr.B: Moïse donna des terres à la tribu des descendants de Ruben, clan par clan.
fr.R: Moïse a donné des terres à la tribu de Ruben, famille par famille.

vi.L: Môi-se đã ban cho chi tộc con cháu Ru-bên theo các gia tộc của họ.
vi.B: Môi-se ban đất cho chi tộc con cháu Ru-bên, theo từng gia tộc.
vi.R: Môi-se ban đất cho chi tộc Ru-bên, theo từng gia đình.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 르우벤 자손의 지파에게 그들의 종족대로 [땅을] 주었다.
ko.B: 모세는 르우벤 자손의 지파에게 종족별로 땅을 주었다.
ko.R: 모세는 르우벤 지파에게 집안별로 땅을 나누어 주었다.

pt.L: E Moisés deu à tribo dos filhos de Rúben, segundo os seus clãs.
pt.B: Moisés deu terra à tribo dos descendentes de Rúben, clã por clã.
pt.R: Moisés deu terra à tribo de Rúben, família por família.

decisions.choice: Moses gave: what he gave is told in what follows
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no object; the next verses spell out the land given. This begins the list of the three eastern shares: Reuben (verses 15-23), Gad (24-28) and the half-tribe of Manasseh (29-31).

decisions.choice: according to their clans: shared out among the clans of the tribe
decisions.reason: The clan was the group of families within a tribe. Each tribe's land was divided among its clans (Numbers 26:5-7, 52-56).

decisions.choice: gave land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "land" as the object of "gave".

decisions.choice: "종족대로" (L); "종족별로" (B); "집안별로" (R) for "according to their clans"
decisions.reason: "종족" is the word Genesis uses in Korean for a clan, the unit within a tribe; Readable says "집안", the plain word, as the English Readable says "family". This holds for chapters 13-24.

decisions.choice: "gia tộc" (Literal, Balanced); "gia đình" (Readable) for the clans of a tribe
decisions.reason: A clan is a large family group within a tribe. Readable uses the everyday word "gia đình", as the English Readable says "family by family".

source.text: וַיְהִ֨י לָהֶ֜ם הַגְּב֗וּל מֵעֲרוֹעֵ֡ר אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֨חַל אַרְנ֜וֹן וְהָעִ֨יר אֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּתוֹךְ־הַנַּ֛חַל וְכָל־הַמִּישֹׁ֖ר עַל־מֵידְבָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And was to them the territory from Aroer, which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi Arnon, and the city which [is] in [the] middle of the wadi, and all the plateau by Medeba;

en.L: And their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the wadi, and all the plateau by Medeba,
en.B: Their territory ran from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, with the town in the middle of the valley and all the plateau by Medeba,
en.R: Their land reached from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River valley, and took in the town in the middle of the valley and all the high plain around Medeba.

sw.L: Na eneo lao lilikuwa kutoka Aroeri, ulio ukingoni mwa korongo la Arnoni, na mji ulio katikati ya korongo, na uwanda wote wa juu karibu na Medeba,
sw.B: Eneo lao lilianzia Aroeri ukingoni mwa Bonde la Arnoni, pamoja na mji ulio katikati ya bonde na uwanda wote wa juu karibu na Medeba,
sw.R: Nchi yao ilianzia Aroeri, ukingoni mwa bonde la Mto Arnoni, ikajumuisha mji ulio katikati ya bonde hilo na nchi yote tambarare ya juu kuzunguka Medeba.

es.L: Y fue su territorio desde Aroer, que [está] a la orilla del torrente Arnón, y la ciudad que [está] en medio del torrente, y toda la meseta junto a Medeba;
es.B: Su territorio iba desde Aroer, a la orilla del valle del Arnón, con la población que está en medio del valle y toda la meseta junto a Medeba;
es.R: Su tierra iba desde Aroer, a la orilla del valle del río Arnón, e incluía el pueblo que está en medio del valle y toda la llanura alta alrededor de Medeba.

fr.L: Et le territoire fut à eux depuis Aroër, qui [est] au bord du torrent de l’Arnon, et la ville qui [est] au milieu du torrent, et tout le plateau près de Médeba,
fr.B: Leur territoire allait d’Aroër, au bord de la vallée de l’Arnon, avec la ville située au milieu de la vallée et tout le plateau près de Médeba,
fr.R: Leur pays allait d’Aroër, au bord de la vallée de la rivière Arnon, et comprenait la ville qui est au milieu de la vallée et tout le haut plateau autour de Médeba.

vi.L: Địa phận của họ là từ A-rô-e, ở bên bờ khe Ạt-nôn, và thành ở giữa khe, và cả cao nguyên gần Mê-đê-ba,
vi.B: Địa phận của họ chạy từ A-rô-e bên bờ thung lũng Ạt-nôn, gồm thị trấn ở giữa thung lũng và cả cao nguyên gần Mê-đê-ba,
vi.R: Đất của họ chạy từ A-rô-e, bên bờ thung lũng sông Ạt-nôn, gồm thị trấn ở giữa thung lũng và cả vùng cao nguyên quanh Mê-đê-ba.

ko.L: 그리고 그들의 지역은 아르논 골짜기 가장자리에 있는 아로엘과 골짜기 한가운데 있는 성읍과 메드바 곁의 모든 평원과
ko.B: 그들의 지역은 아르논 골짜기 가장자리의 아로엘에서부터, 골짜기 한가운데 있는 성읍과 메드바 근처의 모든 평원과
ko.R: 그들의 땅은 아르논 강 골짜기 가장자리에 있는 아로엘에서부터 시작되었고, 그 골짜기 한가운데 있는 성읍과 메드바 둘레의 높은 평원 전체가 들어 있었다.

pt.L: E o território deles foi desde Aroer, que [está] à beira do ribeiro do Arnom, e a cidade que [está] no meio do ribeiro, e todo o planalto junto a Medeba;
pt.B: O território deles ia desde Aroer, à beira do vale do Arnom, com a cidade que fica no meio do vale e todo o planalto junto a Medeba,
pt.R: A terra deles ia desde Aroer, à beira do vale do rio Arnom, e incluía a cidade que fica no meio do vale e todo o planalto em volta de Medeba.

decisions.choice: Aroer, the city in the wadi, the plateau: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: The southern part of the eastern lands, described in verse 9, goes to Reuben. Reuben's land lay north of the Arnon and east of the Dead Sea.

source.text: חֶשְׁבּ֥וֹן וְכָל־עָרֶ֖יהָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּישֹׁ֑ר דִּיבוֹן֙ וּבָמ֣וֹת בַּ֔עַל וּבֵ֖ית בַּ֥עַל מְעֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Heshbon and all its cities which [are] on the plateau: Dibon and Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,

en.L: Heshbon and all its cities that are on the plateau: Dibon and Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,
en.B: Heshbon and all its towns on the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
en.R: It included Heshbon and all the towns around it on the high plain: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,

sw.L: Heshboni na miji yake yote iliyo katika uwanda wa juu: Diboni na Bamoth-baali na Beth-baal-meoni,
sw.B: Heshboni na miji yake yote katika uwanda wa juu: Diboni, Bamoth-baali, Beth-baal-meoni,
sw.R: Ilijumuisha Heshboni na miji yote inayoizunguka katika nchi tambarare ya juu: Diboni, Bamoth-baali, Beth-baal-meoni,

es.L: Hesbón y todas sus ciudades que [están] en la meseta: Dibón y Bamot-baal y Bet-baal-meón,
es.B: Hesbón y todas sus poblaciones de la meseta: Dibón, Bamot-baal, Bet-baal-meón,
es.R: Incluía Hesbón y todos los pueblos que la rodeaban en la llanura alta: Dibón, Bamot-baal, Bet-baal-meón,

fr.L: Heshbon et toutes ses villes qui [sont] sur le plateau : Dibon et Bamoth-Baal et Beth-Baal-Méon,
fr.B: Heshbon et toutes ses villes du plateau : Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Méon,
fr.R: Il comprenait Heshbon et toutes les villes qui l’entourent sur le haut plateau : Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Méon,

vi.L: Hết-bôn và tất cả các thành của nó ở trên cao nguyên: Đi-bôn, và Ba-mốt-Ba-anh, và Bết-Ba-anh-Mê-ôn,

vi.R: Đất ấy gồm Hết-bôn và tất cả các thị trấn chung quanh trên cao nguyên: Đi-bôn, Ba-mốt-Ba-anh, Bết-Ba-anh-Mê-ôn,

decisions.choice: Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon: names that recall the god Baal

records.literal_gloss: and all [the] cities of the plateau, and all [the] kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorite, who reigned in Heshbon, whom struck Moses, him and [the] leaders of Midian, Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, princes of Sihon, dwellers of the land.

en.L: and all the cities of the plateau, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck, him and the leaders of Midian, Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, dwelling in the land.
en.B: all the towns of the plateau, and the whole kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses had defeated him and the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes allied with Sihon who lived in the land.
en.R: It took in all the towns of the high plain and the whole kingdom of Sihon, the Amorite king who had ruled from Heshbon. Moses had defeated him. He had also defeated the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba. They were rulers under Sihon who lived in that land.

sw.L: na miji yote ya uwanda wa juu, na ufalme wote wa Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala Heshboni, ambaye Musa alimpiga, yeye na viongozi wa Midiani, Evi na Rekemu na Suri na Huri na Reba, wakuu wa Sihoni, waliokaa katika nchi.
sw.B: miji yote ya uwanda wa juu, na ufalme wote wa Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala Heshboni. Musa alikuwa amemshinda yeye pamoja na viongozi wa Midiani, Evi, Rekemu, Suri, Huri na Reba, wakuu walioshirikiana na Sihoni walioishi katika nchi hiyo.
sw.R: Ilijumuisha miji yote ya nchi tambarare ya juu, na ufalme wote wa Sihoni, mfalme wa Waamori aliyekuwa ametawala kutoka Heshboni. Musa alikuwa amemshinda. Aliwashinda pia viongozi wa Midiani, Evi, Rekemu, Suri, Huri na Reba. Hao walikuwa watawala chini ya Sihoni walioishi katika nchi ile.

es.L: y todas las ciudades de la meseta, y todo el reino de Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que reinó en Hesbón, al cual hirió Moisés, a él y a los jefes de Madián, Evi y Requem y Zur y Hur y Reba, príncipes de Sijón, que habitaban la tierra.
es.B: todas las poblaciones de la meseta y todo el reino de Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que reinó en Hesbón. Moisés lo había derrotado a él y a los jefes de Madián, Evi, Requem, Zur, Hur y Reba, los príncipes aliados de Sijón que vivían en aquella tierra.
es.R: Incluía todos los pueblos de la llanura alta y todo el reino de Sijón, el rey amorreo que había gobernado desde Hesbón. Moisés lo había vencido. También había vencido a los jefes de Madián, Evi, Requem, Zur, Hur y Reba. Ellos gobernaban bajo Sijón y vivían en aquella tierra.

fr.L: et toutes les villes du plateau, et tout le royaume de Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui régnait à Heshbon, que Moïse frappa, lui et les chefs de Madian, Évi et Rékem et Tsour et Hour et Réba, les princes de Sihon, qui habitaient le pays.
fr.B: toutes les villes du plateau et tout le royaume de Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui régnait à Heshbon. Moïse l’avait battu, lui et les chefs de Madian, Évi, Rékem, Tsour, Hour et Réba, princes alliés de Sihon qui habitaient le pays.
fr.R: Il comprenait toutes les villes du haut plateau et tout le royaume de Sihon, le roi amoréen qui avait régné à Heshbon. Moïse l’avait vaincu. Il avait aussi vaincu les chefs de Madian, Évi, Rékem, Tsour, Hour et Réba. C’étaient des chefs soumis à Sihon qui habitaient ce pays.

vi.L: và tất cả các thành của cao nguyên, và toàn cả vương quốc của Si-hôn, vua người A-mô-rít, là vua trị vì tại Hết-bôn, người mà Môi-se đã đánh, ông ấy và các thủ lĩnh của Ma-đi-an, Ê-vi, và Rê-kem, và Xu-rơ, và Hu-rơ, và Rê-ba, các quan trưởng của Si-hôn, là những người ở trong xứ.

vi.R: Đất ấy gồm tất cả các thị trấn trên cao nguyên và toàn cả vương quốc của Si-hôn, vua người A-mô-rít từng đóng đô tại Hết-bôn. Môi-se đã đánh bại vua ấy. Ông cũng đã đánh bại các thủ lĩnh của Ma-đi-an là Ê-vi, Rê-kem, Xu-rơ, Hu-rơ và Rê-ba. Họ là những người cai trị dưới quyền Si-hôn, sống trong xứ ấy.

ko.L: 평원의 모든 성읍과 헤스본에서 다스리던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼의 온 나라이다. 모세가 그와 미디안의 지도자들, 곧 그 땅에 살던 시혼의 군주들인 에위와 레겜과 수르와 훌과 레바를 쳤다.
ko.B: 평원의 모든 성읍과 헤스본에서 다스리던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼의 온 나라이다. 모세는 시혼과 미디안의 지도자들, 곧 그 땅에 살면서 시혼과 손잡았던 군주들인 에위와 레겜과 수르와 훌과 레바를 쳐부수었다.
ko.R: 그 땅에는 높은 평원의 모든 성읍과 헤스본에서 다스리던 아모리 사람의 왕 시혼의 온 나라가 들어 있었다. 모세는 시혼을 쳐부수었다. 모세는 미디안의 지도자들인 에위와 레겜과 수르와 훌과 레바도 쳐부수었다. 그들은 그 땅에 살면서 시혼 밑에서 다스리던 사람들이었다.

pt.L: e todas as cidades do planalto, e todo o reino de Seom, rei dos amorreus, que reinou em Hesbom, a quem Moisés feriu, a ele e aos líderes de Midiã, Evi, e Requém, e Zur, e Hur, e Reba, os príncipes de Seom, que habitavam na terra.
pt.B: todas as cidades do planalto e todo o reino de Seom, rei dos amorreus, que reinou em Hesbom. Moisés o tinha derrotado, a ele e aos líderes de Midiã, Evi, Requém, Zur, Hur e Reba, os príncipes aliados de Seom que viviam na terra.
pt.R: Incluía todas as cidades do planalto e todo o reino de Seom, o rei amorreu que tinha governado em Hesbom. Moisés o tinha derrotado. Tinha derrotado também os líderes de Midiã, Evi, Requém, Zur, Hur e Reba. Eles eram governantes que estavam sob o poder de Seom e viviam naquela terra.

decisions.choice: the leaders of Midian: the five Midianite kings of Numbers 31:8
decisions.reason: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba are named as the five kings of Midian killed in Israel's war against Midian (Numbers 31:8), after Midian led Israel into sin at Peor (Numbers 25).

decisions.choice: princes of Sihon: rulers bound to Sihon
decisions.reason: The word is used of princes or chiefs and may come from a root linked with pouring out an offering when a ruler was installed. Here it seems to mean that these Midianite chiefs were under Sihon's rule or allied with him, so their defeat belongs to the account of his kingdom.

decisions.choice: leaders: the heads of the Midianite peoples
decisions.reason: The same word names the leaders of Israel's tribes. In Numbers 31:8 the same men are called "kings".

decisions.choice: the princes allied with Sihon
decisions.reason: Balanced says "allied with" for the bare "of Sihon", following m2. Readable says "rulers under Sihon".

decisions.choice: Moses had defeated him ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence at "whom Moses struck" to end the long list.

decisions.choice: os príncipes de Seom (L); os príncipes aliados de Seom (B); governantes ... sob o poder de Seom (R)
decisions.reason: The names of the five Midianite leaders keep the forms of Numbers 31:8 in Portuguese. Their tie to Sihon is not sure (m2): Literal keeps the bare "de Seom", Balanced says "aliados" and Readable "sob o poder de", as the English levels do.

fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} tuèrent aussi par l’épée Balaam, fils de Béor, qui pratiquait la divination, avec les autres qu’ils tuèrent.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont aussi tué par l’épée Balaam, fils de Béor, avec les autres qu’ils ont tués. C’était un homme qui prétendait connaître l’avenir en lisant des signes.
